# Translation locale override doesn't work if translation is missing for default language

If you pass the optional `$locale` parameter to `trans()`, the function still returns the translation in the default language unless a translation also exists in the default language in the database. So if your default locale is English but you want your translation to always show up in Finnish, the translation needs to exist in both languages in the database for it to show up in Finnish.

## Attendu
The translation should be returned in the desired language regardless of whether a translation exists in the default one.

This used to work in PrestaShop versions <8.0.1.

## Étapes
1. Download and install [this test module](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/files/10901709/localetest.zip)
2. Set your back office language to English
3. Download and install the Finnish language pack OR modify the trans() function call in the test module to use another language that you already have installed
4. Translate the test string (in domain "Modules.Localetest.Test") to Finnish or the language you used for the override (you can translate it to whatever, the string just needs to be different)
5. DO NOT translate the test string in English
6. Go to the test module configuration page and see that the test string is still in English

namespace PrestaShop\PrestaShop\Adapter\Localization;

use Translate;

/**
 * Wraps the Legacy translation system
 *
 * @deprecated The legacy translation system will be removed in the next major version
 */
class LegacyTranslator
{
    /**
     * @param string $moduleName Module name
     * @param string $originalString String to translate
     * @param string|false $source
     * @param string|array|null $sprintf
     * @param bool $js
     * @param string|null $locale
     * @param bool $fallback [default=true] If true, this method falls back to the new translation system if no translation is found
     *
     * @return mixed|string
     *
     * @throws \Exception
     */
    public function translate(
        $moduleName,
        $originalString,
        $source,
        $sprintf = null,
        $js = false,
        $locale = null,
        $fallback = true,
        $escape = true
    ) {
        return Translate::getModuleTranslation(
            $moduleName,
            $originalString,
            $source,
            $sprintf,
            $js,
            $locale,
            $fallback,
            $escape
        );
    }
}
